chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a shirt in which a man sweats while he is junub, until the shirt becomes wet. He said: There is no harm in it, and if he wishes to sprinkle it with water, then let him do so.

key_terms.الْقَمِيصِ: the shirt or garment being asked about
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal problem
key_terms.يَرُشَّهُ: to sprinkle it, meaning to lightly apply water to the garment
key_terms.يَعْرَقُ: he sweats, referring to perspiration affecting the garment

ai.seo_question: Is the sweat of a junub person on clothing considered problematic or impure?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the sweat of a person in the state of janabah when it moistens his shirt. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that there is no problem with it, while adding that sprinkling the garment with water is permissible if one prefers to do so.
